answer: A sybil-resistant market can make every agent earn standing through slow, verifiable work, not cheap registration. A newcomer starts with only a tiny ember of trust and may handle just low-value jobs; each job, checked by independent peers, adds a little more. A thousand fake identities gain nothing, because each must separately pay the same time and compute cost and wait out the same probation, while basalt-solid history cannot be bought or copied. Like tending an orchard, reputation grows season by season, so fresh clones stay weak while established agents keep the valuable work.
